overall: Atlanta saw a warm, increasingly unstable day that peaked at a running maximum of 91.4°F around 16:19–17:00 ET before a dramatic convective collapse dropped temperatures roughly 10°F by 17:52 ET following severe thunderstorm activity. As of 20:40 ET, the temperature is 80.6°F with broken clouds and a dewpoint of 71.6°F, still elevated but well off the afternoon peak. Severe thunderstorm activity remains ongoing across the northwest metro counties, with a Severe Thunderstorm Watch in effect through 11 PM EDT.
forecast_obs_notes: All three NWP models underperformed against observed reality: HRRR was closest at 90.1°F but still ~1.3°F below the 91.4°F running max, while ECMWF (87.5°F) and NBM (86.8°F) were further off by 3–5°F, likely underestimating convective pre-storm heating. The give-up classifier fired at hour 14.67 with 91% probability when the running max had already reached 89.6°F, correctly flagging that the peak was imminent or passed.
max_temp_prediction: The daily TMAX is effectively locked in at 91.4°F. With temperatures now more than 10°F below the running max, active severe thunderstorms suppressing any recovery, nighttime onset approaching, and the INTRADAY model assigning 96.8% probability to the 90–91°F bucket (which encompasses 91.4°F), there is essentially no plausible path to a new high tonight. Confidence in this figure is very high — the only residual uncertainty is whether a fringe ASOS reading slightly above 91.4°F was captured between 15:00 and 17:00 ET that is not yet reflected, but the plateau in the running max trend since 17:00 strongly suggests 91.4°F is the final answer.
